question: (a) Differentiate between goodness-of-fit test and the analysis of contingency table.
modelAnswer:
A goodness-of-fit test (e.g., chi-square goodness-of-fit) compares observed frequencies with expected frequencies for a single categorical variable to determine if the data fit a specified distribution.

Analysis of a contingency table (chi-square test of independence) tests whether there is a significant association between two categorical variables using a two-way table of observed frequencies.

question: (b) A die is rolled 420 times with the following outcomes 63, 67, 66, 73, 72, 79. Based on these data, test whether the die is fair at the α = 0.05 level of significance.
modelAnswer:
H₀: die is fair (each face probability = 1/6). Expected frequency per face = 420/6 = 70.
χ² = Σ(O−E)²/E = (63−70)²/70 + (67−70)²/70 + (66−70)²/70 + (73−70)²/70 + (72−70)²/70 + (79−70)²/70
= 49/70 + 9/70 + 16/70 + 9/70 + 4/70 + 81/70 = 168/70 = 2.4.
Degrees of freedom = 6−1 = 5. χ²_critical (α=0.05, df=5) = 11.07.
Since 2.4 < 11.07, fail to reject H₀. The die is fair.

question:
(a) A uniform ladder of length 4m long and of mass 40kg rests with one end against a rough vertical wall and the other end a rough horizontal ground. The coefficient of friction at each point of contact is 0.5. If the ladder is on the point of slipping, calculate the frictional force
(i) of the wall and of the ground
(ii) on the wall
modelAnswer:
At point of slipping: F_W = μR_W = 0.5R_W, F_G = μR_G = 0.5R_G.
Resolving horizontally: R_W = F_G = 0.5R_G.
Resolving vertically: R_G + F_W = mg = 40×9.8 = 392 → R_G + 0.5R_W = 392.
Substitute R_W = 0.5R_G: R_G + 0.25R_G = 392 → 1.25R_G = 392 → R_G = 313.6 N, R_W = 156.8 N.
(i) F_G = 0.5×313.6 = 156.8 N; F_W = 0.5×156.8 = 78.4 N.
(ii) Frictional force on wall = 78.4 N.

Subject to 2x + y ≤ 100, x + 2y ≤ 72, x, y ≥ 0

Feasible region vertices:
(0,0): Z = 0
